outcome: Maternal outcomes (prolonged labor, instrumental delivery, caesarean section, postpartum hemorrhage)
Perinatal outcomes (stillbirth, macrosomia, meconium aspiration syndrome, labour complications, NICU admission, respiratory distress syndrome, intrauterine fetal death)
cohort: The study included 150 cases of pregnancies extending beyond 40 weeks gestation from a tertiary care municipal hospital in East Ahmedabad.
finding: The study found a 46% caesarean section rate in postdate pregnancies, with meconium-stained liquor being the most common indication, and significant neonatal complications including NICU admission in 22% of cases and meconium aspiration syndrome in 13.33%.
mod_finding: The caesarean section rate for postdate pregnancies in this study was 46%, with meconium-stained liquor as the most frequent indication for the procedure.
